maren_root.speaker: Elder Maren
maren_root.text: You have the look of someone who walked here rather than being sent. That is worth more to me than a recommendation.

options.text: Is there something I can do?
I took your letter to the guild.
You said something was gathering them.
Is there anything more I can do?
Is there anything more I can do?

maren_about.speaker: Elder Maren
maren_about.text:
Havenbrook. Sixty-one people, one inn, one forge, and a guild hall that was here before the village was.

The greenwood is east. The Sunken Road runs north to Emberfell, and I would not walk it alone this month. West of the barley is the Mire, and nobody goes there at all.

maren_mire.speaker: Elder Maren
maren_mire.text:
Because the ground there remembers being a graveyard, and it has not forgiven anyone for it.

If you go, and you will, read anything you find before you touch anything you find.

options.text: I will keep that in mind.

maren_letter_offer.speaker: Elder Maren
maren_letter_offer.text:
There is. I have written to the guild and I would rather not trust it to a carter.

Take it up the hill. Put it in the guild master's hand, not on his desk.

maren_letter_accept.speaker: Elder Maren
maren_letter_accept.text: Good. And do not read it. Not because I would mind, but because you would ask me about it, and I would have to answer.

maren_letter_done.speaker: Elder Maren
maren_letter_done.text:
He read it in front of you, then. He would.

Thank you. That was not a small thing, whatever it looked like.

maren_road_offer.speaker: Elder Maren
maren_road_offer.text:
A surveyor went out to the Sunken Road three weeks ago with a satchel full of paper. He came back with the satchel.

He will not say what happened. I would like to know what he wrote down before he stopped writing.

maren_road_done.speaker: Elder Maren
maren_road_done.text:
Let me see it.

...He counted them. Twelve, then thirty, then he stopped counting and started drawing the same shape over and over. That shape is a mine entrance.

maren_depths_offer.speaker: Elder Maren
maren_depths_offer.text:
Orcs do not gather. They raid, they scatter, they raid again. Something under Emberfell is holding them together, and it has been doing it for a season.

The lower workings are locked. The key is somewhere in the upper mine, if the surveyor is to be believed.

options.text: Then I will go down there.
That sounds like a lot of orcs.

maren_depths_accept.speaker: Elder Maren
maren_depths_accept.text: Eat before you go. Take more than you think you need. And if the thing at the bottom talks to you, do not answer it.

maren_depths_done.speaker: Elder Maren
maren_depths_done.text:
You are bleeding on my floor.

Give it here. No, do not explain yet. Sit down first, and then explain.

guildmaster_root.speaker: Guild Master Orlend
guildmaster_root.text: The guild takes contracts, not applicants. If you want work, the board outside is where work lives.

options.text: The letter. Lord Ashcroft is dead, properly.
A letter for the guild, sealed in black wax.
Your ledger mentions a second chamber.
I opened the drowned king's chest.
I brought this out of the barrow.
I will look at the board.

guildmaster_about.speaker: Guild Master Orlend
guildmaster_about.text:
Four of us, down from eleven. We keep the road open, we keep the barrow shut, and we write down what happens so the next four know.

Do the board work. Do it well. Then we will talk about the rest.

guildmaster_letter.speaker: Guild Master Orlend
guildmaster_letter.text:
From Maren? Give it here.

...She is not asking. She is telling me, and she is telling me in writing so I cannot pretend later that she did not.

guildmaster_letter_2.speaker: Guild Master Orlend
guildmaster_letter_2.text:
Something is wrong every year. This year it is counting.

Go back and tell her I read it. She will know what that means.

guildmaster_seal.speaker: Guild Master Orlend
guildmaster_seal.text:
Put it down. On the desk, not in my hand.

You went in there because a note told you to. I want you to hear how that sounds.

guildmaster_seal_2.speaker: Guild Master Orlend
guildmaster_seal_2.text:
It was. That is the part that worries me.

The guild will pay you and the guild will not discuss it further. Take the amulet as well; I would rather it was on someone who can fight.

smith_root.speaker: Smith Halda
smith_root.text: Mind the sparks. The shelf is thin until the ore comes in, but I pay fair for metal -- ore, bars, anything you have hammered into shape.

options.text: I made a helm. It is not a good helm.
Tell me about the workbench again.
The forge is lit. Anything else?
I have an order for you.
Let me see what is for sale.

smith_needs.speaker: Smith Halda
smith_needs.text:
Copper, to start. There is a seam in the foothills north of the barley that nobody has worked in years.

The board has the contract written up properly. Take it from there so it is on paper.

smith_teach.speaker: Smith Halda
smith_teach.text:
I can show you the shape of it, but crafting is hands, not talk. Find a workbench, bring materials, and make something badly. Then make it again.

Here -- two logs and a hide, which is a helm if you are patient and a mess if you are not. Make it, and bring it back so I can see which.

cook_root.speaker: Innkeeper Bess
cook_root.text: Sit anywhere. The fire is lit, and if you have anything raw in that pack you are welcome to use it.

options.text: What happened to the well in the square?
I brought the food you wanted.
I have nowhere to put any of this down.
The house in Mossvale is mine, then.
I brought the fish for the notice.

cook_offer.speaker: Innkeeper Bess
cook_offer.text:
Short-handed and short-stocked. I can cook anything you put in front of me, and there is nothing in front of me.

Bring me five decent cooked portions and I will call us square.

cook_done.speaker: Innkeeper Bess
cook_done.text:
Look at that. Properly done, too, not burnt on one side and raw on the other like the guild lads bring me.

Sit. You are eating before you go anywhere.

cook_rest.speaker: Innkeeper Bess
cook_rest.text: You can. You look like you need it more than you think you do.

guard_root.speaker: Watchman Corrin
guard_root.text: Gate is open, and it stays open. That is the whole job, most days.

options.text: Three boar, and I walked back.
Tell me about the three swings again.

guard_trouble.speaker: Watchman Corrin
guard_trouble.text:
Boar in the barley, orcs on the road, and something in the Mire that the dogs will not walk toward.

So: a normal spring, and two things that are not.

guard_combat.speaker: Watchman Corrin
guard_combat.text:
Three swings, that is all there is.

Quick ones to keep them honest, and they chain if you keep at it -- those teach you to land a blow, which is Attack. A heavy one when you have the room -- those teach you to land it hard, which is Strength, and a held one teaches both. Train only the one and you will either miss a great deal or tickle them. And if you hold the heavy swing and let it build, it comes out hard enough to move something bigger than you. Watch the meter, not the enemy, or you will let go early.

That is the telling. The doing is out of this gate and into the meadow: there are boar in it, and a boar will teach you more in a minute than I will in a week. Put three of them down and come back and tell me which swing did it.

options.text: Three boar. I will be back.

hunter_root.speaker: Hunter Ivo
hunter_root.text: Quiet. There is a deer forty paces behind you and you have already lost it.

options.text: Tell me about meat and fire again.
What is worth taking out here?

hunter_teach.speaker: Hunter Ivo
hunter_teach.text:
Hides come off anything with fur. Meat comes off anything at all. Cook it before you eat it, unless you enjoy the Mire from the inside.

Any fire will do -- the inn has a range, and there is a ring of stones at every camp. Stand at it, press use, pick what to cook. You will burn some to begin with. Everybody does. It stops.

That is the lesson. It is not a long one. Here is some of mine: cook three pieces and come back, and if you ruin it all the meadow is full of more.

hunter_game.speaker: Hunter Ivo
hunter_game.text:
Hare if you are hungry. Deer if you are patient. Boar if you are armoured, and not otherwise.

Fox will fight you for no reason at all. I respect it and I still shoot it.

bram_root.speaker: Bram the Woodcutter
bram_root.text: Mind the fire. And the axe. And the boar, while you are minding things.

options.text: Is something wrong on the trail?

bram_offer.speaker: Bram the Woodcutter
bram_offer.text:
Boar. Big ones, off the verges and onto the trail, and they do not move for a loaded cart. I lost a wheel last week and nearly a mule.

Thin them out. Six should teach the rest.

bram_accept.speaker: Bram the Woodcutter
bram_accept.text: Good. They come out where the trail runs close under the trees. You will hear them before you see them.

bram_active.speaker: Bram the Woodcutter
bram_active.text: Still hearing them at night. Keep at it.

bram_done.speaker: Bram the Woodcutter
bram_done.text: Carts through twice this week without a scream between them. That is your doing. Mossvale owes you a drink, and I owe you a better one.

options.text: I will hold you to it.

bram_about.speaker: Bram the Woodcutter
bram_about.text:
Timber camp. We fell the oaks up here and float them down to Mossvale when the stream is high. The rest of the year we cut, stack, and argue about whose turn it is to cook.

The fork is east of here. Mossvale straight on, Fernhollow up the north path.

oona_root.speaker: Oona the Herbalist
oona_root.text: Mind the pots. Everything on that shelf is either a cure or a poison, and the labels fell off in the damp.

options.text: Could you teach me to brew?
Is there anything you are short of?
I have what you asked for.

oona_offer.speaker: Oona the Herbalist
oona_offer.text:
You could, if your legs are younger than mine. Old Wendel in Fernhollow has a chest that rattles like a cart, and this is the only thing that quiets it.

Take the north path at the fork. He will be on the jetty. He is always on the jetty.

options.text: I will take it to him.

oona_accept.speaker: Oona the Herbalist
oona_accept.text: Tell him it is two spoons, not the bottle. He will not listen, but tell him.

oona_waiting.speaker: Oona the Herbalist
oona_waiting.text: Fernhollow is up the north path at the fork. Two spoons, not the bottle.

oona_rest.speaker: Oona the Herbalist
oona_rest.text:
Sit by the stove. The salve stings, which is how you know I have not given you the roof moss by mistake.

There. Restored, and fit for the trail.

oona_done.speaker: Oona the Herbalist
oona_done.text: He took it? And did he say thank you, or did he say it tasted of ditch? The second one is how I know it is working.

oona_herbs.speaker: Oona the Herbalist
oona_herbs.text: Feverfew, comfrey, and a moss that only grows on the north side of the lodge roof. Reeve Hadley complains about me climbing up there. I complain about his roof.

wendel_root.speaker: Old Wendel
wendel_root.text: Quiet on the jetty. The fish can hear you think.

options.text: I brought the fish you asked for.
The pond is biting for me.
I will leave you to it.

wendel_remedy.speaker: Old Wendel
wendel_remedy.text:
Two spoons, she says. Every time, two spoons.

Tell her it tastes of ditch. She likes to hear it.

wendel_fish.speaker: Old Wendel
wendel_fish.text: There are fish. Whether they are for catching is a question the pond has not answered in forty years.

wendel_ferry.speaker: Old Wendel
wendel_ferry.text: There was a ford south of here, before the stream moved. I ran the ferry. Now I run the jetty, which is the ferry without the going anywhere.

hesper_root.speaker: Hesper
hesper_root.text: Wipe your boots. Wendel never does, and I have given up on him, but not on visitors.

options.text: What are the lights on the pond?
I have been where the lights come from.
The lights are brighter every night.
About the thing in the dream.
It is dead. Here are the shards.

hesper_rest.speaker: Hesper
hesper_rest.text:
The kettle is on. Leave your boots by the door and take the chair by the hearth.

For a little while, there is only the fire and rain against the shutters.

options.text: I feel ready for the road again.

hesper_lights.speaker: Hesper
hesper_lights.text: You have seen them too, then. Mira says the water remembers. Wendel says it is marsh gas. I say both of them should come in before dark.

mira_root.speaker: Mira of the Shrine
mira_root.text: Speak softly by the stones. Not for their sake. For mine.

options.text: The locket. The drowned are quiet.
I found a locket in the Bayou. It knocks.
What are the lights on the pond?
About the voice in the dream.
I found the voice in the dream.
I heard the voice. It said the dream lasts as long as the night.
Shards from the dream, for the shrine.
Could you teach me the shrine's craft?

mira_offer.speaker: Mira of the Shrine
mira_offer.text:
An offering. The hunters used to leave the first of the season here, before they stopped coming north. Two boar haunches, and the pond will stop sulking.

The boar are along the Whisperwood.

mira_accept.speaker: Mira of the Shrine
mira_accept.text: Raw, mind. The water does not care for cooking.

mira_waiting.speaker: Mira of the Shrine
mira_waiting.text: Two haunches. The boar are thickest where the trail runs under the trees.

mira_done.speaker: Mira of the Shrine
mira_done.text:
Mira lays the offering on the worn stone. For a moment the pond is perfectly still.

That will do. Whatever it remembers, it knows we have not forgotten.

options.text: I will leave you to it.

mira_about.speaker: Mira of the Shrine
mira_about.text: It was here before the hamlet, and before the trail. The old words on it say the water remembers. Remembers what, nobody wrote down, which I have always thought was either careless or wise.

mira_enchant_teach.speaker: Mira of the Shrine
mira_enchant_teach.text:
The stones remember. A thing can be made to remember too, if it is asked properly.

Lay a pair of boots on the table by the stones, with a shard of dream and two sprigs of brookmint, and tell them what you want of them. They will carry you quicker after. That is Swiftness, and every other charm starts from knowing how to ask.

options.text: A shard, two sprigs of mint, and ask.

mira_enchant_more.speaker: Mira of the Shrine
mira_enchant_more.text:
Every charm past the first is written down somewhere, the way the brews are. Oona has the one for warding. The traders in Havenbrook and Mossvale keep others, and the strangest are only sold where you go when you sleep.

Work them here, at the table by the stones, or at the one the dream keeps by its candles. Every charm has a craft of its own to it -- Enchanting -- and grows stronger the better you know it. A piece will only take the one.

magister_root.speaker: Magister Orrin
magister_root.text:
Mind the circle. It is older than the floor it is cut into, and it does not care for boots.

The college is fuller than it has been in my lifetime -- a court, a practice hall, a lecture room -- but the books remember when it was more, and the circle remembers further back than the books.

options.text: Could you teach me the old magic?
What does the copying room sell?

magister_teach.speaker: Magister Orrin
magister_teach.text:
The elements are what the land lends you. The old magic is what people wrote down before they had the elements to lean on, and it lends nothing: it takes.

Stand in the circle. Hold the staff as if it were heavier than it is. The word is not said so much as let go of -- there. That was an Eldritch Blast, and every other page in the library starts from it.

magister_more.speaker: Magister Orrin
magister_more.text:
It sits beside the elements, not among them: the fifth mark under your hand, and the same mark again to turn the page. Nothing resists it and nothing fears it.

The rest are in the copying room, at a price that keeps the roof on. Some of them I will not sell to anyone the pond has not spoken to.

magister_about.speaker: Magister Orrin
magister_about.text:
A college, on paper. The tower was here when Fernhollow was three houses; the hamlet grew up round it the way moss grows up a stone. We teach whoever climbs the trail with a staff and the patience for it, which is not many.

The lights on the pond are not ours, whatever Hesper says.

hadley_root.speaker: Reeve Hadley
hadley_root.text: Reeve Hadley. If you are here about the tanner's debts, I am not in. If you are here about work, the notices are by the well.

options.text: What is happening in the Whisperwood?
I will look at the notices.

hadley_mossvale.speaker: Reeve Hadley
hadley_mossvale.text: Timber and hides, and a lodge older than anyone's grandfather. We sell oak to Havenbrook and buy back everything else at twice the price, which Pell will tell you is the natural order of things.

hadley_wood.speaker: Reeve Hadley
hadley_wood.text: The animals are wrong this year. Foxes hunting in packs, boar out on the trail in daylight. Sela thinks something is driving them. Bram thinks it is the weather. I would like it to stop before the timber does.

options.text: I will keep my eyes open.

sela_root.speaker: Warden Sela
sela_root.text: Warden Sela. You came up the trail? Then you already know more about it than the reeve does.

sela_warn.speaker: Warden Sela
sela_warn.text: Foxes in threes now, where there used to be one. They go for the legs. Keep your back to a tree and make them come to you.

pell_root.speaker: Pell the Trader
pell_root.text: Pell. Buyer, seller, and very occasional liar. The carts from Havenbrook have stopped, so the stall is half what it should be.

pell_carts.speaker: Pell the Trader
pell_carts.text: Orcs on the Sunken Road, is what I hear. Nobody wants to haul cloth past that for Mossvale prices. If you are going back that way, tell them we still pay in oak.

tamsin_root.speaker: Tamsin
tamsin_root.text: Tamsin. I trap for the lodge. Or I did, until the foxes started taking the traps as well as what was in them.

tamsin_traps.speaker: Tamsin
tamsin_traps.text: Chewed through the chains. Foxes do not chew through chains. Something is wrong in the wood this year, and I am not the only one who thinks so.

maren_not_yet.speaker: Elder Maren
maren_not_yet.text:
Not yet. What I have for you next would get you killed as you are.

Keep your head down, keep your sword arm busy, and come back to me when the road stops frightening you.

oona_return.speaker: Oona the Herbalist
oona_return.text: He took it? And did he say thank you, or did he say it tasted of ditch? The second one is how I know it is working.

smith_orders.speaker: Smith Halda
smith_orders.text: Orders. I keep a book of them: ore, bars, blades, plate, and more hides than you would think. A few come in every morning. Ask me and I will read you what is open.

cook_daily_logs.speaker: Innkeeper Bess
cook_daily_logs.text: Stack them by the door. No, the other door. That one.

cook_daily_fish.speaker: Innkeeper Bess
cook_daily_fish.text: Minnows! Flour, salt, hot fat. You are staying for some, whether you like it or not.

hadley_daily_hides.speaker: Reeve Hadley
hadley_daily_hides.text: Four. That is four fewer debts on the tanner's slate, which is four fewer conversations I have to have.

pell_daily_oak.speaker: Pell the Trader
pell_daily_oak.text: Seasoned, too. My buyer will not ask where it came from, and I will not tell him it came from you.

wendel_fish_later.speaker: Old Wendel
wendel_fish_later.text: Is it. Is it now. Well, do not tell it I said so, but you have the hands for it.

mira_dream_offer.speaker: Mira of the Shrine
mira_dream_offer.text:
Not lights. Windows. The water remembers, and what it remembers is a place you can only walk into asleep.

Lie down after dark -- a bed, a camp, anywhere under a roof or the sky -- and you will go there. Something there has been trying to speak. Find it, and come back and tell me what it said.

mira_dream_accept.speaker: Mira of the Shrine
mira_dream_accept.text: It is. Do it anyway. And if you die there, you only wake up -- but it takes the rest of your night.

mira_dream_waiting.speaker: Mira of the Shrine
mira_dream_waiting.text: Sleep after dusk. Look for the voice where you arrive. It will not come looking for you.

mira_dream_done.speaker: Mira of the Shrine
mira_dream_done.text:
As long as the night. And that nothing there can kill you, only wake you.

That is a kind thing for a voice to say. I do not trust kind things that live in the water.

mira_daily_shards.speaker: Mira of the Shrine
mira_daily_shards.text: Warm, still. Lay them in the water, one at a time. Slowly.

hesper_dreamed.speaker: Hesper
hesper_dreamed.text:
Then you know more than Mira and less than you think.

Come and see me when you have been back a few times. I have something to ask, and I would rather ask someone who knows the way.

hesper_brute_offer.speaker: Hesper
hesper_brute_offer.text:
Brighter, and closer together. Like something is pulling them in.

Mira will tell you it is the water remembering. I will tell you that I have lived by water all my life and water does not pull. Something in that dream is big, and it is holding the rest of it together. Put it down, and bring me proof I can hang over the door.

hesper_brute_accept.speaker: Hesper
hesper_brute_accept.text: South, Wendel says, from where you arrive. Wendel has never been. Wendel talks in his sleep.

hesper_brute_waiting.speaker: Hesper
hesper_brute_waiting.text: The lights were bright again last night. It is still there.

hesper_brute_done.speaker: Hesper
hesper_brute_done.text: Warm. They are warm. Give them here -- and sit down, you look like you walked all night, which I suppose you did.

tobin_root.speaker: Tobin the Grocer
tobin_root.text: Thread, rods, a fish for the road. If you have something to be rid of, I will take it -- I will not pay much, mind.

options.text: Do you buy anything at all?

tobin_about.speaker: Tobin the Grocer
tobin_about.text: Anything that is not stolen, and some that is. A general store pays a little for everything. Take metal to Halda and fish to Bess and they will pay you better; bring it to me when you cannot be bothered to walk.

garrow_root.speaker: Garrow the Smith
garrow_root.text: Iron from the south road, coal from wherever I can get it. Buying or selling?

options.text: What would make that anvil sing?
Why an anvil out in the open?

garrow_about.speaker: Garrow the Smith
garrow_about.text: The lodge will not have the noise indoors. Out here I can see the trail, and whoever comes up it with ore to sell. Once the wardens have the woods in hand, the azuryte carts will come through again, and I will have that too.

nell_root.speaker: Nell the Pedlar
nell_root.text: Fernhollow has twelve people and one shop, and you are looking at it.

nell_about.speaker: Nell the Pedlar
nell_about.text: For what you cannot carry any further, yes. For fish, Wendel pays better than I do -- do not tell him I said so.

hob_root.speaker: Hob the Pedlar
hob_root.text: Resting the feet. The pack is open, if you want anything from it.

options.text: Let me look in the pack.

hob_about.speaker: Hob the Pedlar
hob_about.text: Mossvale, then Fernhollow, then back to Havenbrook, and round again. Everything I sell costs a little more out here. You are paying for the walk.

options.text: Let me look in the pack.

night_pedlar_root.speaker: The Night Pedlar
night_pedlar_root.text: Welcome to the market that is only open while you sleep. Mind the prices; they are real.

options.text: Do you take coin, in a dream?

night_pedlar_about.speaker: The Night Pedlar
night_pedlar_about.text: Coin you went to sleep with, and coin you will wake with. Whatever you buy here comes back with you, the same as the shards do.

collector_root.speaker: The Collector
collector_root.text: Shards, gems, things with a dream still in them. I buy what others will not look at, and I sell what others cannot find.

options.text: Where does it all come from?

collector_about.speaker: The Collector
collector_about.text: Deeper in than you have been. When the voice by the candles has spoken to you, and when the brute on the lower plateau has stopped troubling Hesper's pond, I will open the better cases.

smith_order_filled.speaker: Smith Halda
smith_order_filled.text: Let me see. Weight's right, work's right. Here -- and there will be more on the book tomorrow.

wendel_order_filled.speaker: Old Wendel
wendel_order_filled.text: Now those are fish. Put them in the basket. I will want more tomorrow, I always do.

oona_brew_teach.speaker: Oona the Herbalist
oona_brew_teach.text: Sit. Two marigolds, a vial of clean water, and a slow fire under the cauldron -- never a quick one. Stir it until it goes the colour of the flower. That is a healing draught, and every other brew starts from knowing it.

options.text: Two marigolds, a vial, a slow fire.

oona_brew_more.speaker: Oona the Herbalist
oona_brew_more.text: Marigolds grow in the open meadows, mint by the water, nettles under the trees. The rarer things grow where the land is strange: the Mire, the high foothills, the burnt ground in the east, and places you only reach asleep. Every brew beyond the first is written down somewhere. I sell the mana tonic; ask the traders for the rest.

cook_cellar_offer.speaker: Innkeeper Bess
cook_cellar_offer.text: Downstairs? Don't. Rats in the grain sacks, and something with too many legs has webbed up the kegs. My boy went down for a barrel and came back up without the barrel. The hatch is behind the bar.

cook_cellar_accept.speaker: Innkeeper Bess
cook_cellar_accept.text: Bless you. Mind the back corner -- whatever spun those webs is the size of a dog.

cook_cellar_waiting.speaker: Innkeeper Bess
cook_cellar_waiting.text: I can still hear them down there. Scratching. The hatch is behind the bar.

cook_cellar_done.speaker: Innkeeper Bess
cook_cellar_done.text: Clear? The big one too? Then you're drinking free tonight, and here -- take something hot for the road.

sawyer_root.speaker: Sawyer Jessa
sawyer_root.text: Mind the sawdust. That log has been on the trestles since dawn and it is winning.

options.text: The sign says an axe is provided.
Here. Ten logs, cut and carried.

sawyer_offer.speaker: Sawyer Jessa
sawyer_offer.text: Provided, lent, and wanted back with interest -- the interest being ten logs. There is a stand of young oak behind me, and a bronze axe in the crate that nobody is using. Bring me ten logs and the axe stops being mine.

sawyer_teach.speaker: Sawyer Jessa
sawyer_teach.text:
Simple enough. Carry the axe -- in your pack is enough, you need not hold it. Walk up to a tree until the prompt reads Chop, then press use. You swing until the wood gives, a log goes in your pack, and you keep swinging until you walk away or press use again.

Every log is Woodcutting experience. The higher that gets the faster you cut, and a better axe cuts faster still -- though an axe of good metal wants the Woodcutting level to match. The young oak behind me is the easiest wood there is: anyone can cut it. A full-grown tree is slower and worth more.

sawyer_accept.speaker: Sawyer Jessa
sawyer_accept.text: There. Mind your shins, and do not try to cut the big timber on the trail until you have some bark under your nails.

sawyer_waiting.speaker: Sawyer Jessa
sawyer_waiting.text: Ten logs. The stand is right behind me -- the saplings go quickest.

options.text: Tell me again how it is done.
Here. Ten logs, cut and carried.

sawyer_replace.speaker: Sawyer Jessa
sawyer_replace.text: Careless. Here, take this one, and keep hold of it.

sawyer_done.speaker: Sawyer Jessa
sawyer_done.text: Ten, and none of them split. That is better than my last apprentice managed in a week.

sawyer_after.speaker: Sawyer Jessa
sawyer_after.text: Cut where you like now. If you get a good load, the pit buys timber, and a better axe is worth every coin.

pit_root.speaker: Pitmaster Dorn
pit_root.text: Watch the face. It drops loose rock on people who stand about admiring it.

options.text: Someone chalked that a pick is lent here.
Eight copper, out of your own face.
How is the face holding, Dorn?

pit_offer.speaker: Pitmaster Dorn
pit_offer.text: Lent, aye. There is copper in that rock and no one with the arms to get it out. Take the spare pickaxe, bring me eight lumps of copper ore, and we will call the pick paid for.

pit_teach.speaker: Pitmaster Dorn
pit_teach.text:
Carry the pick -- your pack will do. Stand at a seam until the prompt names it, copper here, then press use. You work at it until a lump comes free, and you go on working until you move off or press use again.

Every lump is Mining experience, and the level is what lets you touch the deeper metals: copper at the start, iron soon after, then coal and the blue stuff. A pick of better metal works faster but wants the Mining level to swing it. Take the ore to Halda at the forge -- she smelts it into bars, and that is Smithing, which is a different argument.

pit_accept.speaker: Pitmaster Dorn
pit_accept.text: Good. Copper is soft going; do not start on the iron out in the foothills until your arms know the work.

pit_waiting.speaker: Pitmaster Dorn
pit_waiting.text: Eight lumps of copper. The seams are in the face behind me, and they are all copper -- I checked them myself.

options.text: Tell me again how it is done.
Eight copper, out of your own face.

pit_replace.speaker: Pitmaster Dorn
pit_replace.text: Dropped it down a hole, did you. Take this one.

pit_done.speaker: Pitmaster Dorn
pit_done.text: Eight, and you still have all your fingers. The pick is yours.

pit_after.speaker: Pitmaster Dorn
pit_after.text: Dig where you like. The foothills north of here have iron, and the mine past them has better, if you fancy the company down there.

angler_root.speaker: Angler Sula
angler_root.text: Quietly, if you can. They can hear boots.

options.text: Someone wrote that rods are lent here.

angler_offer.speaker: Angler Sula
angler_offer.text: Lent, and I want paying in fish. There is a spare rod in the boat. Six minnow out of this pond and the rod stays with you.

angler_teach.speaker: Angler Sula
angler_teach.text:
Keep the rod in your pack. Stand on the jetty, or on the bank where the prompt reads Fish the pond, and press use. Give it a few seconds and something takes it; keep standing there and you keep catching until you move or press use again.

A rod asks nothing of you -- no level to use it. Your Fishing level only decides how quickly they bite, and once you are past twenty you will start landing two at a time. Raw fish does nobody any good: cook it on a fire, and it heals better than bread.

angler_accept.speaker: Angler Sula
angler_accept.text: Mind the planks, they are slick. Minnow are in close; the pike sit out where the lilies are.

angler_waiting.speaker: Angler Sula
angler_waiting.text: Six minnow. Off the jetty is quickest, and they are in close today.

options.text: Tell me again how it is done.

angler_replace.speaker: Angler Sula
angler_replace.text: Into the water, I expect. Take the spare.

angler_done.speaker: Angler Sula
angler_done.text: Six. And you kept the jetty clear, which is more than the last one did. The rod is yours.

angler_after.speaker: Angler Sula
angler_after.text: The lake up the road has pike and eel in it, and Wendel down in the market will buy every fish you land.

elder_root.speaker: Elder Vask
elder_root.text: An old man in a rocking chair, a blanket over his knees and a stick across them. The chair goes on rocking. He does not look up when you come in.

options.text: The Rime Key. What kept it is dead.
I found a key with SPIREWATCH scratched on it.
They say something took the Ice Spire.
The dragon is dead. Here is its fang.

elder_grunt.speaker: Elder Vask
elder_grunt.text:
*grunt*

He shifts the stick an inch and goes on rocking. Whatever he is waiting for, it is not you.

elder_offer.speaker: Elder Vask
elder_offer.text:
Now he looks up, and takes his time about it. Shoulders, then hands, then the notches on your gear. The chair stops.

"Took it. Yes. I was nineteen and there were eleven of us -- the Spirewatch, they called us, which was a fine name for eleven people with spears. It came down out of the cloud and it took the summit, and I am the one who came back down to say so. Hoarfang, the wyverns' own grandmother called it."

options.text: I will go up and kill it.

elder_why.speaker: Elder Vask
elder_why.text:
"Because the ones who could are dead, and the ones who are alive are sensible. It does not come down. It does not need to. Everything that lives up there feeds it, and the wyverns nest under it the way chickens nest under a hawk."

"Go past the matriarch's nests and keep climbing. Past the last spire the ground opens out, and that is its ground. Take the cold seriously -- it breathes the mountain at you -- and do not fight it in the open unless you can take a hit that would fold a horse."

options.text: I will go up and kill it.

elder_accept.speaker: Elder Vask
elder_accept.text: "Then bring me a tooth. Not the head, not a scale -- a tooth. I have been telling this village for fifty years what is sitting over their heads, and I would like to put something on the table."

elder_waiting.speaker: Elder Vask
elder_waiting.text:
"Still here. So is it."

He turns the stick over once.

"The track up is off the foothills, north. Past the wyverns. You will know its ground when the wind stops -- nothing sings up there."

options.text: The dragon is dead. Here is its fang.

elder_done.speaker: Elder Vask
elder_done.text:
He takes it in both hands, which shake, and this appears to annoy him.

"Fifty years. Eleven of us." A long pause. "There is money in the guild's box that was set aside for this and never spent. Take it. Take the stones too -- I have no use for them and neither had they."

options.text: They would have wanted it done.

elder_after.speaker: Elder Vask
elder_after.text: "Spirewatch." He almost smiles. "There are two of us now. Sit down sometime and I will tell you the other ten names."

elder_spirewatch.speaker: Elder Vask
elder_spirewatch.text:
"Because the ones who could are dead, and the ones who are alive are sensible. It does not come down. It does not need to. Everything that lives up there feeds it, and the wyverns nest under it the way chickens nest under a hawk."

"Go past the matriarch's nests and keep climbing. Past the last spire the ground opens out, and that is its ground. Take the cold seriously -- it breathes the mountain at you -- and do not fight it in the open unless you can take a hit that would fold a horse."

orlend_hoard_offer.speaker: Guild Master Orlend
orlend_hoard_offer.text:
"It mentions a good deal that I would rather it did not." He turns the ledger round so you can read it upside down, which is his way of saying he has read it a hundred times.

"Forty years ago a party went into that barrow and came out four short. What they wrote is that the passage forked, that the far chamber was under water, and that the man they left down there was wearing the king's own boots when he went in. Now the seal is broken and the water has gone down. Go and find out whether they were lying to cover a bad night's work."

orlend_hoard_what.speaker: Guild Master Orlend
orlend_hoard_what.text:
"A chest, in the far chamber, and nothing else worth the walk. It is the last thing in the barrow that has not been carried off by somebody's grandfather."

"If it is there, open it. Whatever is inside is yours -- the guild's interest is in the ledger, not the leather. Bring me the truth and I will pay for it."

orlend_hoard_accept.speaker: Guild Master Orlend
orlend_hoard_accept.text: "Take a lamp. The far chamber is past the rooms you have already cleared, and whatever is down there has had forty years of quiet."

orlend_hoard_waiting.speaker: Guild Master Orlend
orlend_hoard_waiting.text: "The far chamber. Past the fork, as far in as the passage goes." He does not look up from the ledger. "It waited forty years. It will wait until you are ready."

orlend_hoard_done.speaker: Guild Master Orlend
orlend_hoard_done.text:
He takes the ledger, finds the page, and writes one line across it in a hand that presses hard enough to mark the leaf beneath.

"Then they were not lying. Four men, and the guild sealed the door and called it prudence." He closes the book. "The boots are yours. Wear them where people can see them."

bess_well_offer.speaker: Innkeeper Bess
bess_well_offer.text:
She puts the cloth down, which she does not do for much.

"That well fed this town. Four hundred buckets a day out of it, and a queue from dawn -- every family took their share and nobody ever went short, not in the dry years, not once. My mother drew from it. I drew from it."

"Then the year everything went wrong -- the road, the mine, the things out of the Mire -- it slowed. Then it stopped. We have carted water from the brook for eleven years and the cart costs more every spring. Nobody has been down it, because nobody was mad enough."

bess_well_what.speaker: Innkeeper Bess
bess_well_what.text:
"Water, if there is any justice. Something else, if there is not."

"It is a shaft with steps cut in it and rooms cut off the steps -- the old crews worked it in sections, and the sections went down further than the water ever did. It is pitch black. You will not get ten feet without a lantern."

"I can tell you how the crews made theirs: an iron frame, two bars' worth, and a bit of seasoned wood for the handle. Take it to an anvil. Then get a tinderbox off Tobin and put a flame in it, and hold it in your off hand where it will do you some good."

bess_well_accept.speaker: Innkeeper Bess
bess_well_accept.text:
"Then you will want this written down." She chalks the lantern out on the bar top: frame, panes, wick.

"Two iron bars and a length of wood, at an anvil. Light it before you go down, not after -- there is nowhere down there to strike a flame twice."

options.text: I will bring the water back.

bess_well_waiting.speaker: Innkeeper Bess
bess_well_waiting.text:
"The well is in the square, and the shaft has steps. Take the lantern lit."

She wipes the same patch of bar twice.

"If it is something living in the water, kill it. If it is rubble, shift it. If it is neither, come back up and tell me what it is and we will think again."

options.text: Tell me about the lantern again.

bess_well_done.speaker: Innkeeper Bess
bess_well_done.text:
She does not say anything for a moment. Then she takes the cloth off her shoulder, puts it down, and goes to the door to look at the square.

"Eleven years." She sends the boy out with a bucket. "Sit down. You are eating here tonight and you are not paying for it, and if you argue I will have you thrown out of my own inn."

bess_well_lesson.speaker: Innkeeper Bess
bess_well_lesson.text:
"Water, if there is any justice. Something else, if there is not."

"It is a shaft with steps cut in it and rooms cut off the steps -- the old crews worked it in sections, and the sections went down further than the water ever did. It is pitch black. You will not get ten feet without a lantern."

"I can tell you how the crews made theirs: an iron frame, two bars' worth, and a bit of seasoned wood for the handle. Take it to an anvil. Then get a tinderbox off Tobin and put a flame in it, and hold it in your off hand where it will do you some good."

bess_house_offer.speaker: Innkeeper Bess
bess_house_offer.text:
No, and you have been sorting that pack on my clean tables for a week.

Go up the trail to Mossvale. Bottom end of the village, past the tanning frames, there is a house nobody has been in since the tanner went to the coast. See if it is occupied. I would be very surprised.

If it is not -- he kept the key under a loose stone at the gable end, and he was not a man who changed his habits.

bess_house_whose.speaker: Innkeeper Bess
bess_house_whose.text:
Nobody's. The reeve would rather it had a roof kept on it than stood open to the weather, and you are the only person in the valley who owns more than they can carry.

There is a chest in there. Put things in it. That is all a house is.

bess_house_waiting.speaker: Innkeeper Bess
bess_house_waiting.text: Mossvale. The bottom of the village. Look under the stone at the gable end, not the doorstep -- any fool looks on the doorstep.

bess_house_done.speaker: Innkeeper Bess
bess_house_done.text:
It is. Sweep it out before you fill it up.

And you can stop unpacking that bag on my tables.

orla_root.speaker: Orla the Tanner
orla_root.text: Hides go in stinking and come out worth wearing. Put it on the rail and I will tell you what it is worth.

options.text: What can be made of them?
Let me see what you have.

orla_buys.speaker: Orla the Tanner
orla_buys.text: Anything that had a skin. Rawhide off the deer and boar this side of the Wend. Wolf pelts from the far bank: that is your first proper set. Lizard scale out of the Mire, bear from the Brackenwood. After that you are into things I have had on these frames twice in my life: troll, wyvern, and worse than wyvern.

options.text: I will bring what I find.

orla_sets.speaker: Orla the Tanner
orla_sets.text: A coif, a jerkin and chaps, and gloves and striders for the hands and feet, all cut on a tanner's frame. Mine are there, along the north side, and you may use them. Two hides, four and three, one and two, and thread to sew them. Hide will not stop what plate stops. It does not foul a bowstring either. It is an archer's wear, and it puts weight behind an arrow the way plate does behind a sword arm. It does nothing at all for a swordsman.

isolde_root.speaker: Isolde the Weaver
isolde_root.text: Mind the wheel, it bites. You have the look of someone who wants a robe and does not know what goes into one.

isolde_robes.speaker: Isolde the Weaver
isolde_robes.text: Three things. Cloth: three stalks of flax to the bolt at any bench, or two skeins of spider silk if you have a cellar to clear. Dye: a herb and a vial, in the vat there. Nobody needs teaching to boil a flower. Then cut and sew: a hat, a robe and a skirt, and gloves and slippers to go with them. The herb decides the grade. Marigold is homespun, brookmint is what novices wear, and it goes on up to flowers that only open in dreams. A robe keeps out very little, and it carries a spell further than anything else you can put on.

isolde_flax.speaker: Isolde the Weaver
isolde_flax.text: Field edges. Aldous ploughs right up to the fence and the flax takes the strip he cannot reach. Blue flowers, knee high. You cannot miss it, though the sheep manage.

aldous_root.speaker: Farmer Aldous
aldous_root.text: Three ewes since the new moon. They come over the Wend at night, and the fence is for sheep, not for wolves.

options.text: Juniper's collar. The wolves are dealt with.
I found a collar. The tag says Juniper.
Are those your hives, west of the field?
I am sorry to hear it.

aldous_hives.speaker: Farmer Aldous
aldous_hives.text: Eight of them, and the shed of skeps my father kept. The wolves leave the bees alone, which is more than they do for the sheep. Help yourself to the honey -- they make more in a few hours if you leave them some -- and go slow. They know a fast hand for a thief.

options.text: What is the honey good for?

aldous_honey.speaker: Farmer Aldous
aldous_honey.text: My wife's oats, first of all. Then anybody with a cauldron: it sweetens a draught, and the wards against fire and frost will not hold without it. The bugs that go in with it you will have to catch yourself.

aldous_wolves.speaker: Farmer Aldous
aldous_wolves.text: Grey ones, in twos and threes, all along the far bank. Orla pays for the pelts, so they are worth your while. Do not follow them west, mind. What lives up in the Fells is a wolf the way I am a farmhand.

options.text: I will keep to this side of the fork.

hale_root.speaker: Hale the Trapper
hale_root.text: Walk soft and keep downwind. They hear better than you and they smell better than both of us.

options.text: The circlet. The wolves have backed off.
I found this circlet in the wood.

hale_bears.speaker: Hale the Trapper
hale_bears.text: A bear on all fours is thinking about it. A bear that stands up has decided: get out from under, because all of it comes down at once. The hide is worth the trouble. Orla cuts it into the best leathers a working archer can afford, and I pay fair if you would rather not carry it to Hidewater.

hale_den.speaker: Hale the Trapper
hale_den.text: The den. The old sow has had it longer than I have had this camp, and she has two grown cubs that never left. Past her the trail climbs into the Old Growth, and I do not set traps there. The bears are twice the size and they are not shy. Dire bears, my father called them. He had the limp to show he had met one.

wenna_root.speaker: Wenna
wenna_root.text: Eleven years I have carried water up from the mill pond. Four hundred buckets a day that well gave, and now there is a board over it and a sign that says do not go down.

wenna_well.speaker: Wenna
wenna_well.text: Ask Bess at the inn, she will tell you for the price of a drink. I only know my arms ache.

perrin_root.speaker: Old Perrin
perrin_root.text: Tobin has put his onions up a penny. A penny! I remember when the board had one notice on it and it was about a lost pig.

options.text: I brought the bell's tongue back.
Do you remember a bell at Hollowrest?

perrin_now.speaker: Old Perrin
perrin_now.text: Now it is orcs and wells and a west gate that opens. Wolves on the downs, they say, and a tannery paying for the pelts. In my day the wolves paid us. No, that is not right either. Good day to you.

brask_root.speaker: Watchman Brask
brask_root.text: South gate, west gate, guild hall, and round again. Corrin stands still and I walk. We have agreed it is fair.

options.text: You look like somebody who has heard something.

brask_watch.speaker: Watchman Brask
brask_watch.text: The west road, since they opened it. The Westwold is sheep and wolves as far as the river, and wolves without the sheep after it. North of the fork is the Brackenwood, and nobody goes there for the scenery.

tam_root.speaker: Tam
tam_root.text: Logs down to the forge, charcoal back up, logs down to the forge. Jessa says it builds character. Halda says it builds the fire.

dace_root.speaker: Dace
dace_root.text: Pike at the end of the jetty, if you are patient, and minnow if you are not. Sula will lend you a rod. She lent me this one in the spring.

pip_root.speaker: Pip
pip_root.text: Cannot stop! Notices for the board, a message for the gate, and Master Orlend wants it all done before it was asked for.

carter_root.speaker: Hollis the Carter
carter_root.text: Hides out of Hidewater, cloth back. It is a better road than it was, now the gate is open, but I do not stop at the bridge for anybody. There are men there who would like me to.

options.text: Who would like you to stop?

sorrel_root.speaker: Sorrel
sorrel_root.text: Wolf pelts for Ivo, and then I am back out before the light goes. If you are heading west, cross the Wend in daylight and do not camp on the far bank.

options.text: You look like you want something carried.

sorrel_west.speaker: Sorrel
sorrel_west.text: Downs, and wolves on them. Then a fork. North is bear country. West the ground climbs and turns white, and the wolves up there stand as high as my shoulder. I have seen one. I did not stay to see two.

edda_root.speaker: Watchman Edda
edda_root.text: West gate. It was nailed shut for nine years and now I stand at it all day, which is what they call progress.

edda_west.speaker: Watchman Edda
edda_west.text: Hidewater, first, where the tanner and the weaver are: decent people, and they pay. Then the river. Past the river it is wolves, and I count everyone out of this gate and I like to count them back in.

ilse_root.speaker: Warden Ilse
ilse_root.text: Welcome to Fernhollow. It is a gate, a pond and eleven people, and I am the one who is awake.

options.text: Anything I can do for the gate?

ilse_see.speaker: Warden Ilse
ilse_see.text: Wendel on the jetty sells tackle and buys fish. Nell has her cart by the path. Mira keeps the shrine on the west side, and the old tower past the pond is the college: knock, and mind what you touch.

ilse_quiet.speaker: Warden Ilse
ilse_quiet.text: The foxes on the trail are the worst of it, most nights. I do not mind quiet. Quiet is the job done well.

nessa_root.speaker: Nessa the Tanner
nessa_root.text: Mind the vat. If you have hide, pelt or cloth I will buy it, and if you can cut and stitch I will pay you better for what you make of it.

options.text: How do I learn the trade?
I have an order for you.
Let me see what is for sale.

nessa_teach.speaker: Nessa the Tanner
nessa_teach.text:
The frames are there, and you may use them -- a hide is cut on a frame, not on a carpenter's bench. Hide off anything you kill, thread off me or off Isolde's wheel, and start with coifs -- they are small and nobody minds if the first three are poor.

When you can cut one that is not poor, ask me for the book. I post three orders a day and I pay in coin and in what you learn making them.

nessa_order_filled.speaker: Nessa the Tanner
nessa_order_filled.text: Good. That is honest work, and I will say so to anyone who asks.

wynn_root.speaker: Wynn the Clothier
wynn_root.text: Mind the wheel, it bites. Flax, fleece, silk -- I buy all three, and I pay better for what you have already spun, woven or sewn.

options.text: I have an order for you.
Let me see what is for sale.

wynn_teach.speaker: Wynn the Clothier
wynn_teach.text:
Cloth first. Flax off the riverbank, three stems to a bolt, or a fleece off the farm at Havenbrook, which gives two -- and spider silk if you are the sort who goes into cellars.

Then the bolt, the thread and a pot of dye make the piece: a hat, a robe, a skirt, gloves, slippers. The dye is what sets the colour and the tier, and Oona will sell you the first of them.

Bring me what you make. I post three orders a day and I pay in coin and in the doing of it.

options.text: I will go and spin, then.

wynn_order_filled.speaker: Wynn the Clothier
wynn_order_filled.text: That is a straight seam, and I do not say so often.

marrow_root.speaker: Farmer Marrow
marrow_root.text: Mind the gates. Hens in the first pen, pigs in the second, ewes and the herd at the back. If you want meat, milk or a fleece you may take it the honest way, and if you let the pigs out you are getting them back in.

options.text: I will leave you to it.

marrow_what.speaker: Farmer Marrow
marrow_what.text:
Hens give eggs, and the bird itself if you are quick. The cows give milk and a good side of beef. The ewes are the ones worth your while twice over -- mutton, and a fleece that Wynn over at Mossvale will spin into cloth for you.

Cook it at a fire. Anybody can burn meat; it takes a cook to make a supper that carries you through an afternoon.

marrow_who.speaker: Farmer Marrow
marrow_who.text: The inn, mostly, and the guild when they have people in. The rest goes down the Sunken Road with the carts. It is a small town with a large appetite.

guard_combat_accept.speaker: Watchman Corrin
guard_combat_accept.text: Keep your guard up when they come at you -- a boar charges in a straight line, which is the one kind thing about them. And eat something first.

guard_combat_waiting.speaker: Watchman Corrin
guard_combat_waiting.text: Three of them. They root about under the trees just beyond the gate, and they do not need finding -- get close enough and one will find you.

options.text: Tell me again how it is done.

guard_combat_lesson.speaker: Watchman Corrin
guard_combat_lesson.text:
Three swings, that is all there is.

Quick ones to keep them honest, and they chain if you keep at it -- those teach you to land a blow, which is Attack. A heavy one when you have the room -- those teach you to land it hard, which is Strength, and a held one teaches both. Train only the one and you will either miss a great deal or tickle them. And if you hold the heavy swing and let it build, it comes out hard enough to move something bigger than you. Watch the meter, not the enemy, or you will let go early.

guard_combat_done.speaker: Watchman Corrin
guard_combat_done.text: So you did. Which swing was it? -- No, do not tell me, it is always the heavy one and it is always held too long. You will get the feel of it.

guard_combat_after.speaker: Watchman Corrin
guard_combat_after.text:
Three swings, that is all there is.

Quick ones to keep them honest, and they chain if you keep at it -- those teach you to land a blow, which is Attack. A heavy one when you have the room -- those teach you to land it hard, which is Strength, and a held one teaches both. Train only the one and you will either miss a great deal or tickle them. And if you hold the heavy swing and let it build, it comes out hard enough to move something bigger than you. Watch the meter, not the enemy, or you will let go early.

You have heard all I know, and the boar have told you the rest.

smith_teach_how.speaker: Smith Halda
smith_teach_how.text:
A workbench makes anything of wood; hide is cut on a tanner's frame -- Nessa has three, south-west of here -- cloth is woven, and metal is my business and wants an anvil. Stand at one and press use, and it lists everything you could make and what each wants. What you have enough for is lit, what you have not is red.

Every piece made is Crafting experience, and the better things want more of it before they will let themselves be made. There is a bench on the square, south of my door.

smith_teach_accept.speaker: Smith Halda
smith_teach_accept.text: Two logs and a hide. Do not lose the hide, I am not made of cows.

smith_teach_waiting.speaker: Smith Halda
smith_teach_waiting.text:
A Barkwood Helm: two logs and a hide, at any workbench. There is one on the square.

If you have used up what I gave you, there is more where it came from -- Jessa at the sawpit will lend you an axe, and anything in the meadow with fur on it is wearing a hide.

options.text: Tell me again how a workbench works.

smith_teach_lesson.speaker: Smith Halda
smith_teach_lesson.text:
A workbench makes anything of wood; hide is cut on a tanner's frame -- Nessa has three, south-west of here -- cloth is woven, and metal is my business and wants an anvil. Stand at one and press use, and it lists everything you could make and what each wants. What you have enough for is lit, what you have not is red.

Every piece made is Crafting experience, and the better things want more of it before they will let themselves be made. There is a bench on the square, south of my door.

smith_teach_done.speaker: Smith Halda
smith_teach_done.text: Let me see. -- Mm. Well, you made it, and you made it yourself, and that is more than most who come in asking.

smith_teach_after.speaker: Smith Halda
smith_teach_after.text:
A workbench makes anything of wood; hide is cut on a tanner's frame -- Nessa has three, south-west of here -- cloth is woven, and metal is my business and wants an anvil. Stand at one and press use, and it lists everything you could make and what each wants. What you have enough for is lit, what you have not is red.

Every piece made is Crafting experience, and the better things want more of it before they will let themselves be made. There is a bench on the square, south of my door.

When you are ready for metal, bring me ore and I will show you the anvil.

hunter_teach_accept.speaker: Hunter Ivo
hunter_teach_accept.text: Four, and you need three. That is me being generous about the first one.

hunter_teach_waiting.speaker: Hunter Ivo
hunter_teach_waiting.text: Three pieces, cooked. If you have burnt what I gave you, there are hare and deer past the gate and every one of them is dinner.

options.text: Tell me again how it is done.

hunter_teach_lesson.speaker: Hunter Ivo
hunter_teach_lesson.text:
Hides come off anything with fur. Meat comes off anything at all. Cook it before you eat it, unless you enjoy the Mire from the inside.

Any fire will do -- the inn has a range, and there is a ring of stones at every camp. Stand at it, press use, pick what to cook. You will burn some to begin with. Everybody does. It stops.

hunter_teach_after.speaker: Hunter Ivo
hunter_teach_after.text:
Hides come off anything with fur. Meat comes off anything at all. Cook it before you eat it, unless you enjoy the Mire from the inside.

Any fire will do -- the inn has a range, and there is a ring of stones at every camp. Stand at it, press use, pick what to cook. You will burn some to begin with. Everybody does. It stops.

oona_order_filled.speaker: Oona
oona_order_filled.text: Let me see. -- Yes. That is what I asked for and it is as it should be. Look in again tomorrow; the shelves empty faster than I can fill them.

college_porter_root.speaker: Porter Hobb
college_porter_root.text: Through the arch and you are in the court. The hall is north, the practice hall west, the lecture room east, and the grass is for looking at.

options.text: I thought the college was a tower.

college_porter_what.speaker: Porter Hobb
college_porter_what.text:
The College at Fernhollow. It was here before the hamlet and it will be here after. They teach the four elements to anybody with the wit for it, and the old magic to the few the Magister thinks will not hurt themselves.

Visitors may go anywhere but the council's table.

college_porter_tower.speaker: Porter Hobb
college_porter_tower.text:
That was the copying room, down in the corner of the hamlet. Three of them and a leaking roof. The council voted to open the old court again and nobody has been back to it since.

It is a better walk to work, I will say that.

college_usher_root.speaker: Usher Brandt
college_usher_root.text: The council sits within. You may go in; you may not sit down. Mind the runner, and mind the circle more.

college_usher_council.speaker: Usher Brandt
college_usher_council.text:
Magister Orrin at the head of the table, who keeps the circle and teaches the old magic, and sells staves to those who have earned one. Councillor Ferris on his right, who worries. Councillor Wren on his left, who reads.

There are three more chairs. They are for whoever is next.

college_apprentice_root.speaker: Apprentice Tam
college_apprentice_root.text: Can't stop -- hall to the practice hall and back, all day. Do you know how far it is across this court? I do. I have counted.

options.text: Where do your robes come from?

college_apprentice_robes.speaker: Apprentice Tam
college_apprentice_robes.text:
Wynn, at Mossvale. She has a proper shop now, up the lane north-west of the square, gowns in the window. Every hat, robe and skirt in this court came off her loom -- and the dye is what sets the tier, so you will want Oona the herbalist as well.

If you can weave, she keeps an order book. The college is most of it.

college_adept_root.speaker: Adept Sorrel
college_adept_root.text: You are looking at the violet. It means I have been let near the old magic, which means the Magister thinks I will not set fire to myself. He is mostly right.

college_adept_old.speaker: Adept Sorrel
college_adept_old.text:
From him, in the hall, one working at a time, when your Magic is up to it -- and not before, he can tell. It is its own thing: it neither beats the four elements nor is beaten by them. You choose it like a fifth.

Bring coin. Knowledge is free and the Magister's time is not.

college_reader_root.speaker: Apprentice Isa
college_reader_root.text: Water douses fire. Fire scorches earth. Earth smothers air. Air disperses water. Water douses -- sorry. There is an examination.

options.text: What is it worth, getting it right?

college_reader_worth.speaker: Apprentice Isa
college_reader_worth.text:
More than half again. Throw the element a creature fears and the blow is worth sixteen parts where it was ten. Throw the one it is made of and you have wasted your mana and its time.

Lizardmen are water. I got that one wrong in the Mire, once.

college_gardener_root.speaker: Old Peverell
college_gardener_root.text: Four lawns, sixty yards of box, and students. The box I can manage.

college_gardener_statues.speaker: Old Peverell
college_gardener_statues.text:
The founders. Four of them, one to a lawn, each with a staff and a book, and if anybody ever knew which was which it was not written down anywhere I can reach with a rake.

The crystals light themselves at dusk. Nobody knows how that works either. I do not ask.

college_instructor_root.speaker: Battlemaster Ysolde
college_instructor_root.text: Walk where you like. Nothing thrown in this room touches anybody: that is the first working any of them learns, and the only one I insist on.

college_instructor_straw.speaker: Battlemaster Ysolde
college_instructor_straw.text:
Because straw does not mind. It is for the hands -- the stance, the release, the aim. It teaches nothing else, and I will not pretend it does: a spell is learned by landing it on something that would rather you had not.

Anyone who tells you they got good throwing fire at a wall is lying, or was, until recently.

college_instructor_crystals.speaker: Battlemaster Ysolde
college_instructor_crystals.text: They give back what is spent in here, so nobody in a lane runs dry. They do it for the college and for nobody else -- do not ask, the answer is no, and they would not fit in your pack.

college_lane_fire_root.speaker: Apprentice Bryn
college_lane_fire_root.text: Fire. It leaves the ground burning where it lands, which is either the best thing about it or the worst, depending on where you were about to stand.

college_lane_arcane_root.speaker: Adept Corvane
college_lane_arcane_root.text: The old bolt. It goes through the first three things in its way and does not care what any of them are made of. Do not talk to me while I am doing this.

college_lane_water_root.speaker: Apprentice Lisse
college_lane_water_root.text: Water goes through the first two things in its way and into the third. If they are standing in a line, I am your friend.

college_lane_air_root.speaker: Adept Marrin
college_lane_air_root.text: Air comes back off a wall. Twice, if you are good. In a mine that is three chances at the same orc -- in here it is mostly a way to startle Bryn.

college_lector_root.speaker: Lector Maud
college_lector_root.text: -- and so each of the four is afraid of exactly one of the others, and is feared by exactly one. You are late. Sit anywhere.

college_lector_cycle.speaker: Lector Maud
college_lector_cycle.text:
Water douses fire. Fire scorches earth. Earth smothers air. Air disperses water. Round it goes.

A creature made of one takes more than half again from the one it fears, and the number comes up in that element's colour, so that even an apprentice can tell. Most creatures are made of something. Find out what before you are standing in front of it.

college_lector_arcane.speaker: Lector Maud
college_lector_arcane.text:
Outside the circle altogether. It fears nothing and nothing fears it, which makes it the right answer when you do not know the question, and the second-best answer when you do.

It is not taught in this room.

college_pupil_a_root.speaker: A pupil
college_pupil_a_root.text: Shh. She can hear a whisper from the orrery.

college_pupil_b_root.speaker: A pupil
college_pupil_b_root.text: Is it true the Reverie goes down? Three ladders, they say, and everything at the bottom of each is worse.

college_pupil_c_root.speaker: A pupil
college_pupil_c_root.text: Do you know what a Meteor costs? Three bolts' worth. I have done the sum four times. I am taking the Warden's branch anyway.

councillor_ferris_root.speaker: Councillor Ferris
councillor_ferris_root.text: Things are abroad at night that were not, a year ago. Wolves on the meadow. The Mire's dead under the trees on the trail. We have had three reports this month and the council has had three opinions.

options.text: I will leave you to it.

councillor_ferris_advice.speaker: Councillor Ferris
councillor_ferris_advice.text:
Keep to the road after dark. They do not come near it, nor near a gate or a camp, and they are gone at dawn. What you kill stays killed until the next night, for what comfort that is.

Or sleep. A bed does not care what is outside.

councillor_wren_root.speaker: Councillor Wren
councillor_wren_root.text: I have been reading about what the great ones leave behind. The first time one is brought down, something of it stays with whoever did it -- a boon, the old books call it. And for those who go back and back, a totem.

councillor_wren_totem.speaker: Councillor Wren
councillor_wren_totem.text:
It wants a ring to stand in, cut in a floor that is your own. Stood there and touched, it lends you the beast's own strength until the next dawn. One at a time: they do not share.

There is such a ring in the old tanner's house at Mossvale, I am told. I have not been invited.

brask_crypt_offer.speaker: Watchman Brask
brask_crypt_offer.text:
Brask stops walking, which Brask does not do.

"Hollowrest. The graveyard out on the Hollowmarch. Somebody went and opened the crypt under it -- cut the bars, the fools -- and now on my round, when the wind is right, I can hear it. Scratching. Something down there doing what the dead are not supposed to do, which is anything."

"The guild will not send anybody for a noise. You are not the guild."

options.text: I will go down and quiet it.

brask_crypt_accept.speaker: Watchman Brask
brask_crypt_accept.text:
"Two floors, the gravedigger says, before the stairs get worse. Put down whatever is walking on the first, and whatever is floating on the second, and I will call that quiet. Nobody is asking you to go to the bottom."

The round starts again. "Nobody is stopping you, either."

brask_crypt_waiting.speaker: Watchman Brask
brask_crypt_waiting.text: "Still hear it. Fainter, maybe. The Vaults first, then the floor below -- the ones that walk, then the ones you cannot quite see."

brask_crypt_done.speaker: Watchman Brask
brask_crypt_done.text:
Brask listens, as if it could be heard from here, and nods.

"I will take your word, and the guild's purse will take mine. Here. And these -- the herbalist says they are for cuts. I say they are for courage."

brask_crypt_after.speaker: Watchman Brask
brask_crypt_after.text: "Quiet since. Quiet as a crypt ought to be." A pause. "I did not mean that as a joke."

carter_toll_offer.speaker: Hollis the Carter
carter_toll_offer.text:
"Men with a rope across the Westwold road and a story about a toll. There is no toll. There was never a toll. There is a man called Dace with a crossbow, and whoever he has drinking with him that week."

"Four of them, last I counted, and I did not stop to count well. Move them on and I will make it worth the walk."

carter_toll_accept.speaker: Hollis the Carter
carter_toll_accept.text: "Out of the west gate and along the road. They sit where the hedges close in -- you will see the rope before you see them. Do not let Dace talk. He is good at it."

carter_toll_waiting.speaker: Hollis the Carter
carter_toll_waiting.text: "Still there? Then I am still going round by the fields, and the fields are killing my axle."

carter_toll_done.speaker: Hollis the Carter
carter_toll_done.text: "Clear? Truly?" Hollis looks west, as if it could be seen from here. "Then take this, and take the meat as well -- my wife cooked for somebody who would be home late, and I will be home early."

sorrel_pelts_offer.speaker: Sorrel
sorrel_pelts_offer.text:
"Something killed, first. Ivo wants white pelts -- greatwolf, off the high ground in the Westwold where the grass goes pale. Big as a pony and they hunt in threes. I take the grey ones; I do not go up there."

"Three pelts. I will pay what Ivo pays me, and a little over, for the part where you are bitten."

sorrel_pelts_accept.speaker: Sorrel
sorrel_pelts_accept.text: "Out of the west gate. The greatwolves keep to the open, north of the road -- they want to see you coming. Let them."

sorrel_pelts_waiting.speaker: Sorrel
sorrel_pelts_waiting.text: "Three, white, and not chewed. Ivo is fussy about chewed."

sorrel_pelts_done.speaker: Sorrel
sorrel_pelts_done.text: Sorrel lays them over one arm and they cover it from shoulder to wrist. "That is a winter of Ivo complaining about the size. Here -- and the focus draughts, for the next thing you go looking for that you should not."

ilse_hags_offer.speaker: Warden Ilse
ilse_hags_offer.text:
"For the gate, no. For the ferry, maybe. Three times this month it has brought folk up from the Bayou who could not say their own names -- one walked into the water smiling, and the ferryman had to pull him out by the collar."

"They all hum the same tune. The Swamp Hags sing it out there to draw you in, and once you have it your feet follow it. I would like four fewer singers."

options.text: Four fewer. I will see to it.

ilse_hags_accept.speaker: Warden Ilse
ilse_hags_accept.text: "Hit them before they finish a verse. What they throw at you turns you round, or makes you want to walk to them -- either way, keep swinging, and it wears off. The Bayou is off the Hollowmarch; the ferryman will tell you it is haunted. The ferryman says a lot of things."

ilse_hags_waiting.speaker: Warden Ilse
ilse_hags_waiting.text: "The ferry came in this morning with a woman humming. Not your fault. Yet."

ilse_hags_done.speaker: Warden Ilse
ilse_hags_done.text: "Four." Ilse says it the way somebody else might say *finally*. "The ferryman will be glad, and louder about it than I am. Take this. And the bitters -- they taste like the Bayou, which is the point of them."

garrow_horns_offer.speaker: Garrow the Smith
garrow_horns_offer.text:
"Heat. More than coal gives. There is an old smith's story -- demon horn, ground to grit and thrown on the fire, burns hot enough to work platinum without the metal laughing at you."

"I do not know if it is true. I would like to. The things that grow them are out on the Ashen Path, past the Hollowmarch, and I am a smith, not a hero. Four horns."

options.text: Four horns. I will bring them.

garrow_horns_accept.speaker: Garrow the Smith
garrow_horns_accept.text: "It is the big ones that grow the good horns. Do not bring me a horn off something I could have trodden on. I will know."

garrow_horns_waiting.speaker: Garrow the Smith
garrow_horns_waiting.text: "The fire is ready. The fire is always ready. It is the horns that are not."

garrow_horns_done.speaker: Garrow the Smith
garrow_horns_done.text: Garrow weighs the horns one by one, sniffs one, and grins. "If this works you have made me the only smith this side of the Hollowmarch who can work platinum. If it does not, you have made me a smith with four horns. Either way, take the bars. I will not be needing the old stock."

hale_den_offer.speaker: Hale the Trapper
hale_den_offer.text:
"She did. The Den Mother. Biggest bear in the Brackenwood, and she knows what a trap is now -- springs them with a stick, or near enough, and eats what is in them. Took my dog when he went to look."

"Her den is in the rocks not far from here. The bears you see on the trail are hers, one way or another. I would not go in. You look like you might."

hale_den_accept.speaker: Hale the Trapper
hale_den_accept.text: "She stands up before she charges. When she stands up, do not be in front of her. That is all I know, and I learned it from a long way off."

hale_den_waiting.speaker: Hale the Trapper
hale_den_waiting.text: "Still hear her at night. Or I think I do. Same thing, when you are trying to sleep."

hale_den_done.speaker: Hale the Trapper
hale_den_done.text: Hale is quiet a long time. "He was a good dog." Then, brisker: "Here. Coin, and a draught to keep your eye steady -- I was saving it for the day I went in myself, and now I will not have to."

sela_bears_offer.speaker: Warden Sela
sela_bears_offer.text:
"Need done. Yes. The lodge buys its hides from trappers out in the Brackenwood, past the Westwold, and the trappers have stopped going in -- the bears are on the paths, in daylight, in twos. So no hides, so the lodge is short, so the reeve asks me why, as though I keep the bears."

"Eight of them off the paths and the trappers will go back. Mind the big one. There is always a big one."

sela_bears_accept.speaker: Warden Sela
sela_bears_accept.text: "Out of Havenbrook's west gate, across the Westwold, and where the trees close in, that is the Brackenwood. Hale the trapper camps in there, and knows where they are thickest."

sela_bears_waiting.speaker: Warden Sela
sela_bears_waiting.text: "The lodge sent a boy to ask again this morning. I told him about you. Do not make me a liar."

sela_bears_done.speaker: Warden Sela
sela_bears_done.text: "Clear?" Sela chalks it on the slate by the gate. "Good. The lodge will have its hides and the reeve will have one thing fewer to ask me about. Take this -- and the trout. The lodge sent it up for whoever did it."

mira_locket_hint.speaker: Mira of the Shrine
mira_locket_hint.text:
She does not take it. She holds her hand over it, flat, as if it were warm.

"Someone wants this back and cannot come for it -- not walking, anyway. Out in the Bayou the drowned get up again. Lay a few of them down, so whoever it is can hear themselves think, and then bring it here. The stones will know what to do with it better than I will."

mira_locket_done.speaker: Mira of the Shrine
mira_locket_done.text:
"Give it here." She works the hinge with a pin until it gives. A curl of hair, tied with thread. She lays it on the shrine stones and says a name under her breath, and the knocking, which you had stopped hearing, stops.

"There. Take what the shrine has. It does not need coins, and I do not need thanking."

perrin_bell_hint.speaker: Old Perrin
perrin_bell_hint.text:
Perrin takes one look at the clapper and sits down on the nearest step.

"The Hollowrest bell. They rang it for burials when I was small, and when they barred the crypt they took it down and hung it inside, over the stairs. So it would ring, see, if anything down there ever got up and walked."

"And somebody has had its tongue out. Well. That tells you who." A look. "Go down and see. And bring that back after -- it wants putting somewhere it can do some good."

perrin_bell_done.speaker: Old Perrin
perrin_bell_done.text: "Not a sound out of the place while you were down there, I expect. That is the trouble with a bell with no tongue." Perrin turns the clapper over. "I will get it to the smith. Hollowrest can have a bell that rings again, and I can have something to talk about that is not onions. Here -- my father dug that amulet out of the churchyard and never knew what to do with it."

orlend_letter_hint.speaker: Guild Master Orlend
orlend_letter_hint.text:
Orlend looks at the seal and does not reach for it.

"Ashcroft. I know the name from the ledger -- the last lord of the house under Hollowrest, dead before my grandparents' time. If that seal is his, and the wax is fresh, then he is not as dead as the ledger says."

"Keep it shut. Go to the bottom of the crypt and find out what he is now. Then bring it back and I will open it with a clear conscience."

orlend_letter_done.speaker: Guild Master Orlend
orlend_letter_done.text:
Orlend breaks the seal and reads it twice.

"An offer. His crypt left alone, and in return, the guild's dead left alone. Signed, on our side, by a Guild Master sixty years gone." The letter is folded, once. "The guild kept its side. You have just ended his. The purse is yours -- and the draughts. Whoever signed this owes you that much."

The letter goes into the grate.

elder_key_hint.speaker: Elder Vask
elder_key_hint.text:
The chair stops.

He does not take it. His hands stay on the stick. "That is the gatehouse key. Tamsin carried it. Tamsin went back up for the others, the night it came down, and did not come back."

"Something was keeping it, you say. Something cold." A long breath. "Then it came down off the mountain with her key and has been sitting on it ever since. Put it down. Then bring me the key."

elder_key_done.speaker: Elder Vask
elder_key_done.text:
He holds the key a long time. It does not melt in his hands either.

"Fifty years I have told that story with the end missing. Now I know it." He sets the key on the blanket over his knees. "Take the purse. And the draughts -- you will be going somewhere cold again, I expect. Your sort always are."

aldous_collar_hint.speaker: Farmer Aldous
aldous_collar_hint.text:
Aldous takes it out of your hand, looks at the tag, and gives it back.

"Juniper. Best dog I ever had, and she went after them on her own the night they took the third ewe. I told myself she had run off." A pause. "You are going to tell me you will deal with them. Deal with them, then. And bring that back after -- I would like to hang it on the gate."

aldous_collar_done.speaker: Farmer Aldous
aldous_collar_done.text: "On the gate, where she used to sit." He hangs it there himself, on the nail by the latch, and stands looking at it. "Take the coin. Take the meat too; my wife will cook more, she always does. Six wolves. It is not enough for Juniper, but it is a start."

hale_circlet_hint.speaker: Hale the Trapper
hale_circlet_hint.text:
Hale turns the circlet over and finds the mark in the wire.

"Mine. I made it for my sister's girl, for the fair. She dropped it running, the day the wolves came into the clearing -- she got up a tree, and we got her down, and nobody went back for the circlet."

"The same wolves have followed my lines ever since, eating what is in the traps. Thin them for me, and I will give it back to her myself."

hale_circlet_done.speaker: Hale the Trapper
hale_circlet_done.text: "Tooth marks and all." Hale bends the wire straight with a thumb. "She will say it is ruined, and wear it anyway. Here -- a pair of rings I pulled out of a wolf's den last spring. Somebody lost them the way she nearly did."
